notes.aatrox-combo-basic: The basic trade combo is Q1 → E to reposition → basic attack → W → Q2 → Q3. Use E immediately after pressing Q to reposition during the cast and land the blade's sweet spot.
notes.aatrox-combo-w: The W combo is Q1 → W → Q2 before the pull → Q3 immediately after the pull. W also reaches targets within Q1's knockup range. If Q1 misses, hold W to avoid wasting it. Land W immediately after Q1's knockup to limit the opponent's time to walk out of the chain area.
notes.aatrox-combo-ult: The teamfight combo is R → Q1 → E → W → Q2 → Q3. R increases attack damage. R increases self-healing. R's duration can only be extended through takedowns. Since R has a short duration, use it just before engaging when you are sure you can force a fight.
notes.aatrox-skill-q-tip: Q must hit with its sweet spot to deal full damage. Q knocks up opponents hit by its sweet spot. Prioritize landing Q1, which has the longest range of the three casts. Q2 and Q3 have visible windups, making them easy for opponents to dodge.
notes.aatrox-skill-e: E can be used to move even while other abilities are in progress. Use E during Q's cast to adjust the position of its sweet spot. E's passive restores health based on damage dealt to champions. Avoid saving E solely for disengaging, so your abilities and empowered basic attacks keep cycling.
notes.aatrox-laning: At levels 1–2, farm safely near your turret, even if you have to give up some CS. From level 3 onward, farm with Q. From level 3 onward, stick to short trades in lane. Use Q3 and W after the opponent has used their tools for fighting back. In losing matchups, Q's damage alone lets you trade, so choose health and regeneration over attack damage to sustain in lane.
notes.aatrox-laning-q-timing: Harass melee opponents with Q as they step forward to last-hit. Land Q's sweet spot during the opponent's basic attack windup to prevent them from dodging or fighting back. Wait for the opponent's last-hit animation before using Q instead of using it on cooldown.
notes.aatrox-phase: Aatrox is often weak at levels 1–2, when Q has a long cooldown. From level 3 onward, with points invested in Q, Aatrox gains strong trading power. Aatrox reaches his peak in the mid game as he builds up ability haste and items. Aatrox often struggles against duelists in late-game 1v1s.
notes.aatrox-situational-armor: If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Cloth Armor or Bramble Vest first. If the opponent deals heavy physical damage, buy Plated Steelcaps earlier. In matchups where you keep getting pushed back, switch to a build that prioritizes armor and health to survive.
notes.aatrox-situational-antiheal: If the opponent's healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. Buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item.
notes.aatrox-teamfight: In teamfights, use W to group opponents and try to hit multiple targets with Q's sweet spot. Avoid accepting 1v1 duels during teamfights. Engage once you and your allies have created a numbers advantage. Follow up allied immobilizing crowd control with Q to reliably land its sweet spot.
notes.vs-aatrox-q: Aatrox relies on Q for most of his damage. Avoiding Q's sweet spot greatly reduces the damage you take. When you see Q being cast, move outside its sweet spot or inside it toward Aatrox. Aatrox's attacks have pronounced windups, giving opponents time to react.
notes.vs-aatrox-w: If W hits you, leave its area within the time limit to avoid being pulled to the center. Running straight backward is the longest escape route out of W's area. Move sideways or toward Aatrox to escape W's area more easily. Save your mobility ability to escape W's area.
notes.vs-aatrox-r: Aatrox gains increased attack damage when he uses R. Aatrox gains increased self-healing when he uses R. R's duration can only be extended through takedowns. When Aatrox activates R, create distance to avoid taking a 1v1. Wait out Aatrox's R, then look to fight again.
notes.vs-aatrox-early: Aatrox turns early advantages into much larger leads. Focus on securing CS without giving up kills early so the matchup improves as the game goes on.
notes.ahri-combo-basic: The basic combo is E → W → Q. W automatically targets Charmed champions first, then enemies Ahri has hit directly, then other targets. Land E first to focus all three W flames on one target. Landing E first guarantees that the follow-up W and Q will hit.
notes.ahri-combo-q: Q hits on both the outward and return paths. Q's orb returns toward Ahri after being thrown. To hit both parts of Q, throw it past the enemy, then immediately move in toward them. Q's return damage is true damage, so the enemy's magic resistance does not reduce it.
notes.ahri-combo-ult: R is a mobility ability that links your combo together. You can use other abilities while dashing with R.
notes.ahri-skill-e: E only affects the first target it hits. Minions block E, preventing it from reaching enemies behind them. To hit an enemy behind minions with E, move around the side or use R to cross the minion line. Ahri's combat effectiveness drops sharply while E is unavailable. Do not waste E.
notes.ahri-skill-w: W deals greatly increased damage to low-health minions. Use W to last-hit minions and clear waves. Using W increases movement speed. Use W's movement speed boost to chase and disengage.
notes.ahri-skill-r: R lets you dash multiple times. Champion takedowns while R is active increase your remaining dashes. Champion takedowns while R is active extend its duration. Save at least one R dash to disengage. If you can secure a kill, use the extra R dash from the takedown to go after the next enemy.
notes.ahri-skill-passive: P restores health each time you kill a set number of minions. Ahri's lane sustain effectively depends on P's healing. Keep up your CS so P's healing can support your trades. P heals more from champion takedowns than from minion kills. Champion takedowns restore R dashes.
notes.ahri-phase: Ahri is weakest without R because she has no mobility ability available. Do not overextend in lane while R is on cooldown. From the mid game onward, as Ahri builds ability power, landing E gives her stronger single-target kill potential.
notes.ahri-laning: Use Q as your main poke tool in lane. Throw Q so it clips the enemy backline minions to clear the wave and poke at the same time. Save E unless you have a kill opportunity or are setting up a gank. When you run out of mana, stop poking and focus on farming.
notes.ahri-laning-roam: After unlocking R, push the lane and roam. Only enter another lane when both E and R are available. If either E or R is unavailable, farm instead of roaming. Ahri's roams depend on landing E.
notes.ahri-teamfight: Ahri is classified as an assassin, but she is also strong in teamfights. Q is easier to land when enemies are grouped together. Use E to draw one enemy toward your allies so they can follow up. Poke with Q from outside the enemy's range without engaging head-on first. While poking, use E when you have an angle to land it.
notes.ahri-teamfight-cleanup: As the fight winds down, use R to chase fleeing enemies. Use W for movement speed while chasing. Decide how far to chase by calculating how many R dashes takedowns will restore.
notes.ahri-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing offsets your combo damage, use Morellonomicon to reduce it. Buy Morellonomicon after completing one core item.
notes.vs-ahri-e: Standing behind minions lets them block Ahri's E. Ahri's damage potential drops sharply without Charm.
notes.vs-ahri-ult: Ahri has no mobility ability available when R is down. Track when Ahri's R will be available again. Time your ganks or engages for when Ahri's R is unavailable.
notes.vs-ahri-q: Ahri's Q hits on both the outward and return paths. After dodging Q's first hit, keep moving out of its return path. Q's return damage is true damage, so magic resistance cannot reduce it.
notes.vs-ahri-fight: Ahri is most vulnerable immediately after using E. Close the gap and attack as soon as you dodge Ahri's E. If you close in after Ahri misses E, her only remaining way to respond is to dash with R.
notes.blitz-combo-basic: The basic combo is to pull with Q, knock up with E, and finish with R. Chain Q, E, and R without gaps to prevent a squishy target from fighting back. Try the combo within your turret's range so the turret attacks too.
notes.blitz-combo-e-prefire: Activate E just before Q hits to immediately knock up the pulled target. Pressing E after Q pulls the target gives them a window to escape with a mobility ability.
notes.blitz-combo-w-e-first: If you are unsure you can land Q, approach with W, knock up with E, then use Q. Use Q while the target is knocked up by E or when they start fleeing. Check that the enemy has used their crowd control before approaching with W. Start your W engage from brush to make your approach less visible.
notes.blitz-combo-e-reset: E resets the basic attack timer. When harassing, use E immediately after a basic attack to land both attacks in quick succession.
notes.blitz-skill-q: Q pulls only the first enemy it hits along its path. Target enemies when they move away from minions so minions cannot block Q. Hide in brush to conceal your Q reach. Avoid spamming Q early, given its high mana cost and long cooldown. If the Q angle is uncertain, hold it to pressure the enemy into retreating.
notes.blitz-skill-w: Use W to approach and escape. W slows you when it ends, making escape harder. W's attack speed boost contributes greatly to attacking objectives. Use your saved W when starting to attack Dragon or Rift Herald.
notes.blitz-skill-r: R has a relatively short cooldown for an ultimate. Use R to push waves. Use R to disrupt enemy sieges. Clear minions with R to create a Q angle. When sneaking up, keep in mind that R's automatic lightning may unintentionally hit an enemy.
notes.blitz-skill-r-hold: Avoid using R immediately in an extended one-on-one fight with no minions. After several hits, R's passive lightning deals more total damage than its active. Use R when you need immediate burst damage. Use R when you need a silence. Use R when you need to remove enemy shields.
notes.blitz-skill-passive: P's shield strength scales with current mana. Save some mana to get a sufficient P shield when in danger. With full mana early on, trust your large P shield and look for opportunities aggressively.
notes.blitz-phase: At level 1, using Q leaves you unable to apply much pressure for a while. Blitzcrank starts applying serious grab pressure at levels 2–3. Blitzcrank stays strong throughout the early and mid game. As the game progresses, Blitzcrank relies on allied follow-up to kill targets. In the late game, avoid grabs without allied follow-up.
notes.blitz-laning: Blitzcrank's grab opportunities in lane depend heavily on securing brush vision. Control the brush to conceal your grab range. When Q is on cooldown, fall back and protect your ally as they farm.
notes.blitz-laning-invade: Q is especially effective in narrow jungle chokepoints. Join early invades and try to catch the enemy jungler with Q at chokepoints. Look for chances to steal enemy camps with Q during early invades. If your lane is stable, pressure enemy jungle routes with your allies.
notes.blitz-teamfight: Blitzcrank struggles to kill healthy targets alone and relies on allied damage. Engage with Q only when allies can follow up immediately. After engaging, use E and W to stick to the target and maintain pressure.
notes.blitz-situational-thornmail: If the enemy's main damage is physical and they also have healing, choose Thornmail for both armor and healing reduction.
notes.vs-blitz-minion: Q pulls only the first target it hits along its path. Stand behind minions rather than beside them so they block Q.
notes.vs-blitz-cooldown: Q costs a lot of mana at level 1. Q has a long cooldown at level 1. Use the window immediately after a missed level 1 Q to pressure the lane or trade.
notes.vs-blitz-mana: Q costs a lot of mana. Watch Blitzcrank's mana bar to identify safe windows when he cannot use Q.
notes.vs-blitz-peel: Blitzcrank lacks the damage to finish off targets with crowd control alone. Bypass Blitzcrank and engage on his allies behind him. When enemies bypass Blitzcrank to attack his allies, his ability to protect only one ally becomes a limitation.
notes.vs-blitz-shield: P creates a shield that scales with mana when health gets low. Account for P's shield, secure a way to finish the kill, then try to kill him in one go.
notes.vs-blitz-vision: Giving up brush vision makes it harder to judge grab range. Use Control Wards to secure brush vision. Stay well away from brush when moving through areas without vision.
notes.caitlyn-combo-trap-q: Place W under enemies or where they will retreat. When an enemy triggers W, use Headshot, then Q. Use Q only when the enemy steps out to the side of the minions or gets trapped. Caitlyn's Headshot range is increased against trapped targets.
notes.caitlyn-combo-e-headshot: Headshot range increases against targets hit by E. After landing E, use Headshot, place W where the enemy will retreat, then use Q. Use E to create Headshot opportunities.
notes.caitlyn-combo-e-reposition: Use E's recoil movement to create distance. Use E's recoil movement to escape over walls.
notes.caitlyn-skill-passive: Headshot activates after a set number of basic attacks. Basic attacks from brush charge Headshot faster. Use the Headshot charged while moving in and out of lane brush on champions. Avoid attacking minions when Headshot is fully charged.
notes.caitlyn-skill-q: Q deals progressively reduced damage to targets farther behind the first target. Caitlyn stands still while aiming Q.
notes.caitlyn-skill-w: W stores multiple trap charges. Place W in advance so its cooldown finishes during the fight. Place W where enemies must pass, such as brush entrances, jungle entrances, or behind you.
notes.caitlyn-skill-e-keep: E is Caitlyn's only escape ability. Using E to poke first leaves you without a way to respond to an enemy engage. Save E until you confirm the enemy has used their engage ability.
notes.caitlyn-skill-r: Another enemy champion can take the hit from R instead of its target. Avoid using R in chaotic fights. Use R to finish off a fleeing target, a duel opponent, or an enemy in another lane only when no champion can block its path. Caitlyn stands still while casting R.
notes.caitlyn-phase-early: Caitlyn's long range lets her pressure enemies from level 1, even without items. Caitlyn excels in the laning phase. Build an early lead through CS and turret pressure.
notes.caitlyn-phase-late: In the mid to late game, Caitlyn has less raw damage output than other marksmen with strong sustained damage. Caitlyn reaches her power peak when she converts her lane lead into turrets and objectives. After her power peak, use her range advantage to attack from a safe position.
notes.caitlyn-laning-push: Caitlyn ranks among the best in CS and turret plating metrics. Use your range advantage to push the wave first and keep enemies pinned under their turret. Destroy turret plates while enemies are pinned under their turret. While the wave is pushed, place W at river approaches to defend against ganks.
notes.caitlyn-laning-trade: Only attempt trades when Headshot is ready. Poking with basic attacks without Headshot gives enemies an opening to close in. Back out of range immediately after trading to deny enemies an engage opportunity.
notes.caitlyn-teamfight: Attack from the edge of your maximum range in teamfights. Place W along enemy approach routes and around your feet to block their approach. Secure your position before the teamfight starts. In teamfights, save E exclusively for interrupting enemy engages.
notes.caitlyn-situational-antiheal: If the enemy team has a lot of healing, buy Executioner's Calling after completing one core item. Caitlyn's range lets her attack throughout teamfights and continuously apply Executioner's Calling's healing reduction.
notes.vs-caitlyn-q: Q pierces targets, dealing progressively reduced damage to targets farther back. When being poked by Q, stand behind allied minions so they take the first hit.
notes.vs-caitlyn-r: R hits an allied champion of the target instead if they block its path. If an ally is targeted by R, step into the bullet's path to protect them.
notes.vs-caitlyn-rooted-cast: Caitlyn stands still while casting Q. Caitlyn stands still while casting R. When you see Q or R's cast animation, close in or find an angle to attack. The moment after Caitlyn uses Q to clear the wave is the best time to engage.
notes.vs-caitlyn-e: E is Caitlyn's only escape ability. E moves Caitlyn through recoil. Engage after Caitlyn uses E, when she has no way to create distance.
notes.vs-caitlyn-phase: Caitlyn is strongest during the laning phase and becomes relatively weaker as the game goes on. Avoid taking excessive risks early and giving Caitlyn kills.
notes.darius-combo-basic: The basic trade combo is E → auto attack → W → Q. Landing E guarantees an auto attack and W. Use W's auto attack reset to quickly reach three Hemorrhage stacks. Finish the combo with Q, taking half a step back to land the blade.
notes.darius-combo-execute: The execution combo is E → auto attack → auto attack → W → Q → auto attack → R. R damage scales with the target's Hemorrhage stacks. Use R after reaching maximum Hemorrhage stacks. E's slow keeps the enemy in range while you add auto attacks.
notes.darius-skill-passive: Hemorrhage stacks up to five times. Reaching maximum Hemorrhage stacks greatly increases attack damage. Alternate auto attacks and abilities to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Darius grows stronger as fights drag on and he builds Hemorrhage stacks. Back off from fights that started with no Hemorrhage stacks.
notes.darius-skill-q: Q deals full damage only to enemies hit by the blade. Q's healing scales with the number of enemy champions and large monsters hit by the blade. In lane, step back as you use Q to hit the enemy champion with the blade. Using Flash during Q's cast moves the blade's hitbox.
notes.darius-skill-w: W resets the auto attack timer. W applies a strong slow to the target. Use W immediately after an auto attack to build Hemorrhage stacks quickly. Slow fleeing enemies with W to keep them in Q and R range. Avoid spending W on minions so you don't miss out on Hemorrhage stacks on champions.
notes.darius-skill-e: Use E right after the enemy uses their mobility ability. You cannot use Flash during E's cast. For a surprise engage, use Flash before E. E's passive grants armor penetration. Give lower priority to penetration-focused items whose effects overlap with E's armor penetration.
notes.darius-phase: Darius is weak at levels 1–2, when he has few abilities available. Darius gets stronger at level 3 with W and Q available, and at level 6 when he gains R. Darius has low item dependence and stays strong through the mid game. Darius is vulnerable in prolonged wars of attrition against ranged poke opponents. Darius falls off in standard late-game teamfights where he struggles to engage. Use your lane advantage during your strong periods to secure gains.
notes.darius-situational-armor: Buy Plated Steelcaps early if the enemy deals mostly physical damage. If the enemy deals mostly physical damage, choose Dead Man's Plate or Randuin's Omen for armor and slows that help you chase.
notes.darius-situational-magic: If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Mercury's Treads to reduce the time you spend immobilized. If the enemy deals mostly magic damage, buy Force of Nature after Mercury's Treads. Roots and stuns can easily disrupt Darius's combo. Prioritize tenacity over magic resistance when roots or stuns interrupt your combo.
notes.darius-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing turns fights around, buy Executioner's Calling between core items. Darius relies on extended brawls and can easily lose his edge against sustained enemy healing.
notes.darius-laning: Freeze the wave on your side to lure the enemy into E range when they go for minions. Land E from brush or in narrow terrain to follow up with your combo. After pushing the wave, secure vision against ganks before moving forward.
notes.darius-teamfight: Darius struggles to reach backline damage dealers, putting him at a disadvantage in head-on teamfights. In narrow terrain, pull multiple enemies with E, then hit them together with Q's blade to heal. Getting a kill with R resets its cooldown. Start a kill chain by targeting enemies you can reliably finish with R. If you cannot make use of narrow terrain, apply pressure in a side lane through 1v1s.
notes.vs-darius-e: Poke Darius from outside his E range. Save mobility abilities and Flash to respond to Darius's E. Start a trade when Darius misses E or it is on cooldown.
notes.vs-darius-passive: Darius's attack damage rises sharply when Hemorrhage reaches maximum stacks. Create distance from Darius if Hemorrhage stacks are building up. Hemorrhage stacks expire over time. Stay away from Darius until Hemorrhage stacks expire, then reengage.
notes.vs-darius-q: Darius heals more based on the number of enemies hit by Q's blade. When you see Q being cast, move outside the blade's range to prevent damage and healing. When you see Q being cast, move close to Darius to get hit by the handle and reduce damage and healing. Poke Darius right after he uses Q to clear minions.
notes.vs-darius-r: Darius's R deals true damage. Darius's R damage increases with the target's Hemorrhage stacks. If Darius gets a kill with R, its cooldown resets. If you have several Hemorrhage stacks and your health is dangerously low, move completely out of R range.
notes.vs-darius-phase: Repeat short, hit-and-run trades to deny Q healing and maximum Hemorrhage stacks. Darius relies on W's slow to disengage. Once you gain a favorable position against Darius, keep pressuring him, as he relies on W's slow to escape. Darius is strong in early skirmishes and dives. Watch out for skirmishes and dives when the enemy jungler joins Darius.
notes.fiora-combo-basic: For short trades, Q toward a vital → auto → E. E empowers the next two basic attacks. E's second basic attack is a guaranteed critical strike. When a new vital appears while E is active, hit it with the second empowered auto attack.
notes.fiora-combo-vital-angle: If a vital appears on the opponent's back or side, use Q to dash in that direction and hit it. Hit front-facing vitals with auto attacks and E, and save Q to chase or disengage. Hitting a vital grants movement speed, making it easier to move toward the next vital. Look for an angle to hit two vitals in succession during a single fight.
notes.fiora-skill-vital: Hitting a passive vital deals true damage based on the opponent's maximum health. Hitting a passive vital restores health. Vitals reappear in a different position after a set time or when hit. If the current vital is at a difficult angle to hit, wait for the next one instead of forcing an engage. The true damage from vitals is not reduced by the opponent stacking armor.
notes.fiora-skill-q: Q dashes in the chosen direction and attacks the nearest enemy. Q prioritizes hitting a vital if one is within its hit area. Hitting an enemy with Q greatly reduces its cooldown. Using Q without hitting anything does not reduce its cooldown. When using Q to move, make sure to hit something, even a minion or ward.
notes.fiora-skill-riposte: W blocks all attacks during its brief cast time. W blocks immobilizing effects during its brief cast time. If W blocks an immobilizing effect, its counterthrust stuns instead of slowing. Save W until the opponent has to use immobilizing crowd control. Simply having W available discourages the opponent from using abilities.
notes.fiora-skill-e: E increases attack speed. E's first empowered auto slows the opponent. E's second empowered auto is a guaranteed critical strike. Hit a vital with E's second empowered auto attack. Use E after setting up a situation where you can stay close enough to land both empowered autos.
notes.fiora-phase: Fiora gets stronger in 1v1s as she gains items. Avoid reckless fights early, looking ahead to 1v1s after scaling. Fiora is weak in large teamfights. Fiora excels at gaining advantages through split pushing.
notes.fiora-situational-antiheal: Fiora fights by hitting vitals one after another, gradually wearing down her opponent's health. Fiora struggles to duel opponents who use sustained healing to recover the damage between vital hits.
notes.fiora-laning: After hitting a vital, use the increased movement speed to create distance. Trade to bait out the opponent's mobility ability first and gain an advantage in mobility usage.
notes.fiora-laning-vs-physical: If the opponent has strong physical damage trades, focus on minimizing early losses rather than winning lane. In unfavorable physical damage trading matchups, stay in experience range even if you have to give up some minions. In unfavorable physical damage trading matchups, let the wave come toward your turret. Starting in the mid game, once your items come together, force 1v1s in a side lane. Once Fiora scales, she can turn around matchups that were unfavorable early.
notes.fiora-teamfight: Choose side lane pressure over large fights. R reveals four vitals on the target. Use R in 1v1s or skirmishes where it provides the most value.
notes.fiora-teamfight-ult: R's vitals deal true damage based on the opponent's maximum health. Hitting all four R vitals or killing the target heals you and nearby allies.
notes.vs-fiora-riposte: When facing Fiora, bait out W first. Fiora's W blocks all incoming attacks and immobilizing effects during its cast. If Fiora blocks an immobilizing effect with W, her counterthrust stuns. Avoid using immobilizing abilities such as roots or stuns while Fiora's W is available. Sidestep when using key abilities to avoid getting hit by Fiora's W.
notes.vs-fiora-riposte-aatrox: Fiora will try to block Aatrox's third Q cast or W pull with W. Use Aatrox's first and second Q casts to bait out Fiora's W. After baiting out Fiora's W, use Aatrox's third Q cast and W. Save Aatrox's W while Fiora's W is available.
notes.vs-fiora-vital: The vital marked on your body signals the direction Fiora intends to attack from. Position on the opposite side from the marked vital to narrow Fiora's approach angles. Counterattack the moment Fiora dashes toward the vital. Do not overcommit to chasing Fiora after a short trade.
notes.vs-fiora-ult: When Fiora uses R, hug a wall. Covering one vital with a wall can prevent Fiora from hitting all four R vitals. If Fiora hits all four R vitals, she and her nearby allies heal.
notes.vs-fiora-late: Fiora is strong in late-game 1v1s. In the late game, take down Fiora in a side lane with at least two players instead of facing her alone. In the late game, force teamfights instead of dueling Fiora in a side lane. The true damage from vitals is not reduced by stacking armor.
notes.garen-combo-basic: For a basic trade, silence with a Q-empowered auto attack, then use E. Q's movement speed boost helps you close in on your opponent. Deal damage with E while Q's silence prevents your opponent from retaliating with abilities.
notes.garen-combo-e-first: If your opponent is already close, use E before Q. You can use Q during E to silence without interrupting the spin. Save Q until your opponent starts using an ability to fight back.
notes.garen-combo-ult: To finish your opponent, use a Q-empowered auto attack, then E, recast E to end it early, and use R. R deals true damage proportional to your opponent's missing health. If your opponent shows no sign of escaping, let E deal its full damage before using R. If your opponent shows signs of escaping, recast E to stop it and immediately use R.
notes.garen-skill-q: Q removes all slows affecting Garen. Garen has no mobility ability, so he relies on Q to chase. Use Q right after your opponent slows you to remove the slow. Q's empowered auto attack remains available briefly after activation. You can activate Q outside attack range, then approach and silence with the empowered auto attack.
notes.garen-skill-w: W's shield and tenacity apply only for a very brief moment right after casting. W's damage reduction lasts longer than its shield and tenacity. Time W for the moment an enemy ability comes at you. W's passive permanently increases armor and magic resistance whenever you kill a unit. Secure last hits in lane to build up W's defenses.
notes.garen-skill-e: E hits more times during its spin with higher attack speed. E's damage can critically strike. To increase E's total damage, mix in attack speed and critical strike chance instead of building only attack damage. E reduces the armor of champions it hits multiple times. To support allied physical damage dealers, let E spin for its full duration to reduce enemy armor. E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy. During trades, position so only the enemy champion is within E's range.
notes.garen-skill-passive: P restores health after some time without being hit by a champion. Minion attacks do not interrupt P's healing. After a trade, briefly retreat into a brush or behind a turret to heal with P. P's healing lets Garen hold his lane even in unfavorable matchups.
notes.garen-phase: Garen's base health and P healing make him strong in early melee trades. Garen peaks in the mid game when Q's duration increases and R reaches rank 2. In the late game, as enemies become more durable, Garen relies on R's execute more than E's damage. Use lane pressure and split pushing to secure your advantage in the mid game.
notes.garen-situational-onhit: E's spin damage does not apply on-hit effects. Items whose value centers on on-hit effects, such as Blade of the Ruined King, are less efficient because those effects do not apply to E. For the same cost, choose attack speed and critical strike items that work well with E.
notes.garen-situational-boots-slow: If the enemy team has many slows, choose Boots of Swiftness over Berserker's Greaves to close in more easily while Q is on cooldown. You cannot use Q to remove slows while it is on cooldown.
notes.garen-situational-mr: If enemy magic damage is a threat, swap your boots for Mercury's Treads, which provide magic resistance and tenacity. Garen is vulnerable to being locked down by crowd control while E spins without hitting anyone.
notes.garen-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing is a problem, buy Mortal Reminder earlier to get healing reduction. If healing reduction is more urgent, buy Executioner's Calling first. Without healing reduction, Garen struggles to trade against opponents who heal through E's sustained damage.
notes.garen-laning: Let the wave push toward you instead of pushing it. Garen has no mobility ability, leaving him vulnerable to ganks when his lane is pushed. Always keep wards available to prepare for ganks. Trade when your opponent steps forward to last-hit a minion. After pushing the wave with E, retreat into a brush to activate P's healing.
notes.garen-teamfight: Garen cannot take the initiative in starting teamfights. Once your allies start the fight, move in while timing W. In teamfights, hold the front line and use E to reduce enemy armor. Use R in teamfights when an enemy's health drops. To avoid being kited, look for an opening to reach the enemy backline from the flank or out of vision. If there is no opening for a teamfight, split push and sustain with P without recalling to keep one enemy tied down in a side lane.
notes.vs-garen-q-cooldown: Garen's Q-empowered auto attack silences you, preventing retaliation with abilities. Start a trade right after Garen uses Q on a minion or consumes its empowered auto attack. Avoid approaching Garen while his Q is active.
notes.vs-garen-silence: Garen's Q silence interrupts abilities with long cast times and channeled ultimates. Use abilities with long cast times or channeled ultimates after Garen has used his Q silence.
notes.vs-garen-e: Garen's E deals continuous damage while he spins. Garen's E deals bonus damage to the nearest enemy. Avoid extended fights with Garen and keep taking short, hit-and-run trades. If you cannot leave E's range, move among allied minions so a minion becomes the nearest enemy. Avoid approaching Garen in a brush so you do not take the full damage of E's spin.
notes.vs-garen-w: Right after using W, Garen briefly withstands burst damage and crowd control with a shield and tenacity. When you see Garen activate W, delay your combo slightly.
notes.vs-garen-r: Garen's R deals true damage proportional to his opponent's missing health. Armor and magic resistance cannot reduce Garen's R damage. Stay outside Garen's R range when your health falls below half. Champions who fight while recovering from low health through life steal must be especially wary of Garen's R execute.
notes.vs-garen-mobility: Garen has no mobility ability. Garen has limited ability to leave his lane and influence other lanes. Push the wave hard to expose Garen to jungle ganks. After pushing the wave in, create a numbers advantage elsewhere.
notes.graves-combo-engage: Close the gap with E, then basic attack at point-blank range. E loads one shell into the magazine. Use E just before reloading to keep attacking without interruption. At point-blank range, cut off their vision with W, then use Q.
notes.graves-combo-q-wall: Q explodes immediately when it hits terrain. Against an opponent with their back to a wall, hit the wall with Q to land the explosion quickly. Against an enemy across a wall, fire Q right against the wall to land the explosion.
notes.graves-combo-r: R explodes again in a cone behind the champion it hits. Line up R when other enemies are lined up behind the target. Casting R knocks Graves backward. Use R's recoil to cross a wall while escaping.
notes.graves-skill-passive: After using both shells in the magazine with basic attacks, you start reloading. Each basic attack fires a spread of pellets. Basic attack pellets are all blocked by the first unit they hit. Find an angle with no units between you and the target, then get close.
notes.graves-skill-q: Q's follow-up explosion deals much more damage than its outgoing projectile. Aim Q slightly ahead or to the side so the opponent stays in the explosion area even if they dodge the projectile. At jungle camps, hit a wall with Q so the explosion covers the entire camp.
notes.graves-skill-w: When ganking, place W on the opponent's escape route to help your allies chase.
notes.graves-skill-e: Using E toward an enemy champion grants twice as many armor stacks. Each basic attack hit reduces E's cooldown. Keep landing basic attacks so you can use E twice in one fight. Do not carelessly spend E on an early escape and lose your engage tool and armor.
notes.graves-phase: Graves is strong in level 2–3 fights. Learning R at level 6 gives you a finishing tool, increasing your gank success rate. Graves is vulnerable to being taken down easily if caught first in the late game. Graves reaches his peak strength in the early to mid game. Secure objectives and vision in the early to mid game to cement your lead.
notes.graves-laning-route: Graves farms efficiently thanks to his fast jungle clears. At camps with plenty of walls, hit a wall with Q to clear faster. If a gank opportunity is unclear, clear camps to widen the level and gold gap.
notes.graves-laning-gank: Gank when the opponent is past the middle of the lane and your ally has a way to lock them down. Use E to close down the angle, then throw W onto the opponent's escape route. Throwing W first cuts off vision, preventing your allies from landing their abilities too.
notes.graves-teamfight: In teamfights, do not initiate from the front. Once your allies draw the enemy's attention, use E to move in from the side or rear and get close to their damage dealers. Maintain a position with no units between you and the target.
notes.graves-situational-antiheal: Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to reduce healing. Graves concentrates his damage into a short window.
notes.graves-situational-boots: If the enemy's damage is mostly magic, choose Mercury's Treads over Plated Steelcaps to bolster your magic resistance.
notes.vs-graves-block: Graves's basic attacks are fully blocked by the first unit they hit. In chaotic fights, keep minions or allies between you and Graves to block his basic attacks.
notes.vs-graves-reload: After emptying his magazine, Graves cannot basic attack while reloading. Counterattack or create distance right after Graves fires both shells.
notes.vs-graves-smoke: Vision is limited inside W's smoke. Movement speed is reduced inside W's smoke. Leaving W's area immediately removes its harmful effects. Take the shortest route out of W's smoke, then reengage.
notes.vs-graves-q: Q explodes immediately when it touches terrain. Fight in open terrain so you have room to dodge Q's explosion.
notes.vs-graves-armor: Graves deals almost entirely physical damage, making him vulnerable to armor. Buy Plated Steelcaps earlier to counter his early to mid game physical damage.
notes.jax-combo-trade: For short trades, use auto attack → W → auto attack. W resets the basic attack timer. W increases basic attack range. Cancel your auto attack animation with W before it finishes to fit in one more attack in the same time. Hit minions to build passive stacks before trading. After activating R, time W with the bonus damage proc during consecutive attacks to concentrate your burst damage.
notes.jax-combo-engage: Engage with E → Q → recast E mid-leap → auto attack → W → auto attack. Activate E before Q to stun almost as soon as you land, before the opponent can disengage. If you need to guarantee the stun, use Flash and recast E together as soon as E can be recast.
notes.jax-skill-e-core: E dodges all basic attacks except turret attacks for its duration. E's recast damage increases in proportion to the number of attacks dodged. Activate E just as the opponent starts their auto attack animation. E also dodges bonus damage and crowd control carried by basic attacks. You can choose when to recast E. Approach with E active, feint a retreat, then immediately jump in with Q or Flash to reduce the opponent's reaction time. During a gank, activate E immediately when two enemies attack you at once.
notes.jax-skill-e-vs-melee: Jax has the advantage in level 1 trades against melee opponents. E dodges enemy and minion basic attacks, the main sources of damage in level 1 trades. Use the health advantage gained from a level 1 trade against a melee opponent to get through the rest of the laning phase.
notes.jax-skill-e-vs-ranged: Against ranged opponents, save E for an all-in you can reliably win or for responding to a gank instead of spending it on a single poke. After using E against a ranged opponent, stay outside their range until its cooldown ends, even if you have to give up CS. Against ranged opponents, look for opportunities to engage with Q. When engaging a ranged opponent, activate E just before Q so the stun follows your landing.
notes.jax-skill-e-limit: E's dodge only applies to basic attacks. Of ability damage, E only partially reduces area-of-effect ability damage. Against opponents who mainly deal magic damage with abilities, do not assume E will let you withstand their damage. Against opponents who mainly deal magic damage with abilities, activate R as you enter combat to gain armor and magic resistance. Use E to negate the opponent's key basic attacks or crowd control carried by basic attacks.
notes.jax-skill-q: Use Q primarily to engage and disengage rather than to deal damage. Q targets units and can also be used on minions and wards. Use a pre-placed ward as an escape route with Q. Against melee opponents, start trades by moving into range and save Q to chase or disengage. When the opponent advances away from their turret, use Q to land on their retreat path.
notes.jax-skill-r: R's passive deals bonus magic damage on every third consecutive attack. Keep attacking without breaking your auto attack rhythm to make use of R's bonus damage. R's active grants more armor and magic resistance based on the number of champions hit. Use R from a position where it can hit multiple enemy champions. Both W and R have AP ratios. W and R's AP ratios let Jax make efficient use of items that grant both attack damage and ability power.
notes.jax-phase: Jax is strong in level 1 melee slugfests. Jax is weakest at levels 2–5 because he lacks poke, farming abilities, and sustain. Jax gets a sharp power spike at level 6 when he learns R. Jax gets a sharp power spike when he completes his first core item. Late game, with passive stacks and items built up, Jax excels in head-on fights against champions who rely on basic attacks. As the game goes on, Jax lacks damage against tanks who build both health and armor.
notes.jax-situational-item: Choose situational items based on how you are dying. If an enemy auto attack carry is doing well, use Frozen Heart to reduce their attack speed and help you trade blows after E ends. If magic burst kills you before you can act, use Banshee's Veil to block the opening ability. Against a team composition that kills you as soon as you are crowd controlled, use Sterak's Gage to survive.
notes.jax-laning: Aim to get through the laning phase without falling behind. Start trades with passive stacks already built up. When E is on cooldown, farm from outside the opponent's range. Position yourself between the opponent and their turret first to make E and Q easier to land. If you need a safe recall window, use E's recast area damage to push the wave into the enemy turret.
notes.jax-teamfight: Use Q to jump into grouped enemies and stun several of them with E. When entering a teamfight, activate E before leaping with Q. To survive, go in second, following an ally's crowd control or engage. If there is no reason to start a teamfight, push side-lane turrets to draw enemy defenders.
notes.vs-jax-e: Do not use basic attacks while Jax's E is active. Jax's E also dodges bonus damage and crowd control carried by basic attacks. Jax's E deals more recast damage for each attack it dodges. When Jax activates E, back out of its stun range and wait for its duration to end. Save your mobility ability to get out of Jax's E range. Since Jax's E does not block ability damage itself, plan your trades around abilities.
notes.vs-jax-bait: Jax can activate E, feint an approach, then retreat to bait out the opponent's mobility ability or ultimate. Do not spend your escape or defensive ability just because Jax activates E. After Jax's E ends, use its cooldown window to trade. Pressure Jax with your jungler while his E is unavailable.
notes.vs-jax-early: Jax has a weak laning phase because he lacks poke, farming abilities, and healing. Avoid forcing melee trades at level 1, when Jax has the advantage. From level 2 onward, build a CS and level lead over Jax. Secure an advantage before Jax gets stronger by learning R at level 6 and completing his first core item.
notes.vs-jax-ranged: When playing a ranged champion against Jax, whittle down his health with auto attack poke. Even when poking with a ranged champion, stop auto attacking while Jax's E is active. Jax gains attack speed with successive basic attacks, increasing his damage. Repeat short trades instead of prolonged fights to disrupt Jax's basic attack rhythm. Jax can use minions or wards as stepping stones to engage with Q. Avoid standing next to minion groups so Jax cannot use Q to close in. Watch how many allied minions remain in front of Jax while staying outside his Q range.
notes.vs-jax-teamfight: When Jax engages, avoid grouping up nearby so his E's area stun does not hit you together. If Jax engages with E active, use your abilities after E's duration ends. Immediately after Jax's E stun ends, focus crowd control on him to kill him. If Jax pushes a side-lane turret, split your team to pressure his team's territory and trade objectives instead of forcing a duel.
notes.leesin-skill-passive-weave: Flurry increases the attack speed of the next two basic attacks after using an ability and restores energy. When escaping with a ward jump, place the ward over a wall toward your team's side.
notes.leesin-skill-q: Q's first cast is a skillshot projectile blocked by minions and jungle monsters. Approach from the side when ganking so the wave does not block Q. Avoid firing Q into empty space to check vision if you want to preserve your engage tool. Q's first cast grants true sight of the target hit, keeping them visible even if they flee into brush.
notes.leesin-skill-q2-timing: Q's second cast deals more damage the more health the target is missing. Use allied CC and basic attacks to lower the target's health first, then finish with Q's second cast. When delaying Q's second cast, use it before its short recast window expires.
notes.leesin-skill-w: W dashes to allies and your own wards. Place a ward over a wall to create a W path for an engage from an unseen angle. Before placing a ward, decide whether to use it for a W engage or escape.
notes.leesin-skill-w-recast: W's second cast increases omnivamp. Use W's second cast to sustain your health while clearing jungle camps and heal during skirmishes. Use W's second cast as you start basic attacking immediately after engaging.
notes.leesin-skill-e: E's first cast deals area damage around you and provides stealth detection. Use E's first cast to check unwarded brush or reveal a hidden opponent. E's second cast slows opponents. Use E's second cast after the opponent uses their escape ability to chase them.
notes.leesin-skill-r: R holds the target in place during its cast. The target knocked back by R knocks up other enemies they collide with. Use R to kick the opponent toward your allies. To knock up multiple enemies, kick R's target through a group of enemies.
notes.leesin-combo-basic: The basic gank combo is Q's first cast, basic attack, E's first cast, basic attack, then Q's second cast, adding E's second cast if needed. Weave Flurry-empowered basic attacks between abilities in your gank combo. Use Q's second cast in your gank combo after lowering the opponent's health.
notes.leesin-combo-ward-jump: To ward jump, place the ward first, then use W before the ward lands. To approach from outside Q range, place a ward over a wall or behind the opponent and use W to dash to it.
notes.leesin-combo-insec: To perform an Insec, land Q's first cast, approach with Q's second cast, get behind the opponent, then use R to kick them toward your allies. To perform a ward Insec, land Q's first cast, use a ward and W to get behind the opponent, then use R to kick them toward your allies. To change R's direction with Flash, start casting R, then Flash during the cast.
notes.leesin-combo-r-q2: If your allies are far away, land Q's first cast, use R to kick the opponent toward them, then follow with Q's second cast. Hold Q's second cast until after R so you can close the gap created by the kick.
notes.leesin-phase-early: Lee Sin is strongest in early jungle duels and counter-jungling. Look for a chance to disrupt the enemy jungler's route immediately after clearing your first two or three camps. From level 6, when R becomes available, look for opportunities to break open a lane with an Insec.
notes.leesin-phase-late: Lee Sin's damage contribution drops as the game goes on, making solo kills harder. In the late game, use R to separate one enemy so your strong allied carry can fight more easily. In the late game, use R to knock away opponents who dive your backline.
notes.leesin-laning: Plan your jungle route to turn your early strength into an advantage. Steal camps or influence a lane when the enemy jungler is tied up on the opposite side. Keep in mind that you have no escape tools immediately after using both Q and W. Save W to escape when going deep into the enemy jungle.
notes.leesin-teamfight: Only engage when your allies can follow up immediately. If your allies have not engaged yet, save R to knock away an enemy engager. Lee Sin has limits to how long he can hold the frontline in teamfights. Before entering a teamfight, plan an escape route using W or Q's second cast.
notes.leesin-situational-antiheal: Against opponents who sustain through healing, buy Executioner's Calling between core items to capitalize on your early dueling advantage. Upgrade Executioner's Calling to Mortal Reminder to reduce the healing of opponents who rely on it to survive.
notes.vs-leesin-q-block: Most of Lee Sin's engages depend on landing Q's first cast. Lee Sin's first Q cast is a projectile blocked by minions and jungle monsters. If you expect a Lee Sin gank, keep the wave between you and him to block Q's straight path.
notes.vs-leesin-ward-jump: Lee Sin can cross walls by using W on his own wards. Watch for Lee Sin engaging with a ward and W from beyond walls where you lack vision. Use Control Wards to clear wards beyond walls and prevent Lee Sin from engaging with a ward and W. Position one space away from the wall to prepare for Lee Sin's ward-W engage.
notes.vs-leesin-q2: Lee Sin's second Q cast deals more damage the more health the target is missing. If Q's first cast hits you while you are below half health, move toward an allied turret or your team during the short window for Q's second cast.
notes.vs-leesin-r-position: If Lee Sin has room to get behind you, watch for the risk of being kicked by R. Position with your back to a wall or your team's frontline so that even if R kicks you, you move toward your allies. If an ally knocked back by Lee Sin's R collides with you, you will also be knocked up. Spread out from your allies just before a teamfight so R cannot knock up multiple teammates together.
notes.vs-leesin-early-duel: Lee Sin is strong in early duels and falls off in the late game. If you encounter Lee Sin in the jungle early, avoid dueling him and retreat. Use objective and lane advantages to buy time until the late game, when Lee Sin falls off.
notes.vs-leesin-w-sustain: Lee Sin heals during skirmishes through the omnivamp from W's second cast. Apply healing reduction if Lee Sin survives longer than expected in extended fights through W's omnivamp. Focus your damage on Lee Sin immediately after he uses W to engage.
notes.lux-combo-full: Use the kill combo in this order: Q → place E → R → auto attack → detonate E → auto attack. Weave auto-attacks between abilities to keep consuming Illumination marks. Delay detonating E so you can land both auto-attacks.
notes.lux-combo-poke: In lane, poke by placing and detonating E, then auto-attacking to consume the Illumination mark. Use Q for kill opportunities or to stop enemy engages rather than for poke. Lux loses her means of fighting back when Q is down.
notes.lux-skill-passive: Illumination marks enemies hit by Lux's damaging abilities. Lux's auto-attacks consume Illumination marks to deal bonus magic damage. R consumes Illumination marks on hit, then reapplies them. After using R, auto-attack to consume the Illumination mark for extra damage. Use auto attacks after landing abilities to deal enough damage.
notes.lux-skill-q: Q fully roots the first two enemies it hits. Angle Q to root both the tank and the carry standing behind them. Lux relies on landing Q to land follow-up abilities and defend herself. Use Q carefully so a miss does not leave you defenseless.
notes.lux-skill-w: W grants a shield on both its outward and return paths. The two shields granted by W stack. Cast W toward grouped allies. While fleeing, cast W in the direction you are running to receive the returning shield sooner.
notes.lux-skill-e-zone: To control an area, place E and delay its detonation. Place E ahead of time on entry or escape routes to hinder enemy movement. Throw E into a brush to check for an ambush. E is Lux's most reliable ability to land. Avoid spamming the mana-heavy E so you do not run out of mana midway through laning.
notes.lux-skill-r: R has a cast time. R displays a red targeting line before firing. Account for R's cast delay so it hits before the root ends. R's cooldown is reduced when Lux gets a takedown. R's short cooldown and takedown cooldown reduction can let you cast it twice in a teamfight.
notes.lux-phase: Look for kill opportunities as early as level 1 if Q's root lands. Treat level 6 as the first power spike, when R lets you finish enemies beyond your range. Lux deals her strongest damage during her mid-to-late-game burst window, after building up ability power. In the late game, prioritize positioning over damage to prepare for enemy assassins closing in.
notes.lux-laning-safety: Lux has no mobility ability. Lux has almost no way to respond when caught in an ambush. Play at maximum range to prepare for ambushes. Check unwarded brush with E before entering.
notes.lux-laning-wave: When support Lux hits minions with E, it pushes the lane and increases the risk of exposure to enemy jungle ganks. When you need to let the wave push toward you, use E so it only hits enemy champions. Use E on the wave only when you need to push.
notes.lux-teamfight: Position behind your team's frontline in teamfights. Use Q to stop enemy engages. Use E to block enemy movement routes. Use W to protect allies from burst damage. To get value for the mana spent, avoid angles that hit only one enemy and use abilities on multiple enemies.
notes.lux-teamfight-ult: R pierces enemies in a straight line. Angle R to pierce grouped enemies in a single line. R's cooldown is greatly reduced when Lux gets a takedown. Use R for a guaranteed finish to get your next R sooner and increase total damage.
notes.lux-situational-assassin: Buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to prepare for enemy assassins closing in. With no mobility ability, Lux relies on W's shield for her own survival when caught.
notes.lux-situational-antiheal: Choose Morellonomicon to reduce healing when enemy healing becomes a problem. E and R apply Morellonomicon's healing reduction to multiple enemies at once.
notes.vs-lux-q: Lux relies on Q's root to guarantee that her remaining abilities land. Treat the moment after Lux misses Q as an opportunity to engage while she is defenseless. Bait out Lux's Q, dodge it, then engage.
notes.vs-lux-q-line: Q roots the first two enemies it hits. Avoid lining up with allies and leave space to the side so Q does not root you together.
notes.vs-lux-e: E hinders access to a specific area. Spread out and approach from different directions so E does not block you all.
notes.vs-lux-r: R displays a red targeting line before firing its main beam. When retreating at low health, avoid fleeing in a straight line to prepare for R. Prepare to dodge sideways as soon as R's red targeting line appears.
notes.vs-lux-passive: Getting hit by Lux's abilities applies an Illumination mark. Lux's auto-attacks consume Illumination marks to deal bonus damage. Move out of Lux's auto-attack range immediately after an ability hits you to avoid Illumination's bonus damage.
notes.vs-lux-squishy: Lux has no mobility ability. Lux struggles to survive when an enemy manages to get close. Find an approach angle from a brush or the flank to get close to Lux.
notes.malphite-combo-trade: For short trades against melee opponents, activate W and attack in this order: basic attack → E → basic attack. W empowers your next basic attack and makes each basic attack leave an aftershock for the next few seconds. Use E after the opponent starts a basic attack to reduce their retaliation.
notes.malphite-combo-ult: Use R → W → basic attack → Q → E for your ultimate burst combo. Q and E are guaranteed to hit while R's knockup lasts. Activate W immediately after R to empower the basic attack you weave between abilities.
notes.malphite-skill-armor-scaling: Both W and E deal damage that scales with armor. W's passive increases Malphite's armor. W's armor bonus increases greatly while Granite Shield is active. Armor items improve both survivability and W and E damage, so avoid leaving them out of your build entirely.
notes.malphite-skill-passive: Granite Shield regenerates only after you take no damage for a certain time. Start trades with Granite Shield charged. Back off and recharge Granite Shield when it breaks. Higher armor reduces the amount of Granite Shield depleted by physical attacks. Approach melee opponents while using Granite Shield to absorb their first basic attack.
notes.malphite-skill-e: E deals area damage to enemies within its range. E reduces the attack speed of enemies it hits. Use E immediately after a basic attack-focused opponent starts attacking. Save E until you have a target to fight instead of using it on cooldown to farm.
notes.malphite-skill-r-utility: R makes you unstoppable during the cast, ignoring most crowd control as you dash to the target location. Use R as an escape tool when fleeing a gank. Use R to dodge incoming skillshots by passing through them. Given R's long cooldown, decide in advance whether to use it to escape or save it to engage. Build ability haste to poke with Q and use R more often.
notes.malphite-phase: Malphite is weakest before level 6, when he has no R. Malphite's limited mana restricts how often he can poke early on. Take advantage of the power spike immediately after learning R. Take advantage of your peak strength in the mid game, when you have two or three armor items. Your damage contribution drops late in the game, so focus on starting teamfights with R.
notes.malphite-situational-armor: If the enemy's main damage is physical, focus on armor items that improve both survivability and W and E damage. Against physical damage, buy Glacial Buckler early, then build into Plated Steelcaps, Thornmail, Frozen Heart, and Randuin's Omen. If the enemy has plenty of healing, finish Thornmail first to apply Grievous Wounds.
notes.malphite-situational-mr: If the enemy's main damage is magic, choose Hollow Radiance for magic resistance and farming power. Choose Spirit Visage as your magic resistance item if you have allies who provide healing or shields. Choose Force of Nature when taking magic damage from multiple enemies. Keep one armor item for W and E damage even in a magic resistance-focused build.
notes.malphite-situational-ap: Choose an ability power build to secure kills with R when your team has another frontline tank and the enemy backline is squishy. Choose Rylai's Crystal Scepter to keep enemies from getting away after R. Choose Rabadon's Deathcap and Void Staff to increase R's damage. Choose Zhonya's Hourglass to buy time for your allies to join you after you engage with R. Choose Liandry's Torment to apply damage over time to multiple enemies with R.
notes.malphite-laning: During the laning phase, repeatedly poke with Q, then back off to recharge Granite Shield. Q steals the opponent's movement speed, making it harder for them to chase you after you poke. At low Q ranks, time your poke around when you can use a source of mana restoration. Malphite struggles to gain a lead through kills in lane. Extend your lead by pushing the wave and chipping away at turret health.
notes.malphite-teamfight: Only engage when R is available. When enemies group up, find an angle to knock up at least two with R. Look for a chance to kill a key damage dealer with R when they step out alone. Coordinate R's timing with your allies so they can follow up with area-of-effect ultimates at the knockup location.
notes.vs-malphite-r: Malphite's R is an unstoppable dash that cannot be interrupted by crowd control.
notes.vs-malphite-grouping: Malphite's R knocks up multiple enemies in its dash path at once. Spread out to either side before entering a teamfight to prevent R from hitting multiple teammates. Focus your counterattack immediately after Malphite uses R.
notes.vs-malphite-early: Gain lane control before Malphite reaches level 6, while he has no R and is short on mana. Arrange a jungle gank before Malphite reaches level 6 to delay his scaling. Keep in mind that Malphite becomes harder to beat one-on-one once he has R and armor items.
notes.vs-malphite-passive: Break Malphite's Granite Shield before starting your combo. Prevent Granite Shield from regenerating with damage over time or frequent poke. Avoid starting a trade immediately after Q hits you, since it steals your movement speed. Stand behind minions to block Q and make Malphite waste mana.
notes.vs-malphite-e: E's attack speed reduction lowers the damage output of basic attack-focused champions. As a basic attack-focused champion, stay behind your allies and maintain your range while keeping outside E's range. Move in and attack after Malphite uses E.
notes.wukong-combo-eq: Buffer Q while dashing in with E. Q empowers your next basic attack. Activate Q during the dash to land the empowered attack faster than if you activate it after arriving.
notes.wukong-combo-rw: Use W immediately after starting R. A W clone created immediately after R mimics Cyclone. Use W's invisibility to retreat and avoid the enemy's counterattack.
notes.wukong-combo-r-flash: You can move while casting R. To compensate for R's short range, Flash into the middle of the enemy team while casting it. To knock up multiple enemies with R, reach them before they spread out.
notes.wukong-skill-r: Your movement speed increases during R. Walk into grouped enemies while spinning with R. Use the first R as a signal for your team to engage. Use the second R to finish enemies off or hinder their escape. Stuns and roots interrupt R, so use it after the enemy's main crowd control has been used.
notes.wukong-skill-w: W is a dash that briefly makes you invisible. W leaves a stationary clone where you cast it. Use your W clone to draw targeted enemy abilities away from you. Do not use W immediately after engaging, so you can disappear from enemy vision and disguise your movement direction. W's invisibility is revealed by turrets and true sight.
notes.wukong-skill-q: Q is an empowered basic attack with increased range. Q's armor reduction also increases your allies' physical damage. Q's cooldown decreases whenever Wukong or his clone attacks an enemy. Save Q for champion fights instead of wasting it on a wave or camp beforehand.
notes.wukong-skill-passive: Gain P stacks whenever you attack champions or jungle monsters. P stacks increase your armor. P stacks increase your healing. Attack nearby jungle monsters just before a fight to build up P stacks. Clone attacks also build P stacks.
notes.wukong-skill-e: E is a targeted dash that enemies cannot dodge. E has short range, so first find an opening to get close to the enemy. Do not use E first while the enemy still has their mobility ability available. Follow up with basic attacks immediately after E lands to use the increased attack speed.
notes.wukong-phase: Wukong's early clear speed and damage per minute are average. Wukong is especially vulnerable to magic damage. Build an advantage through early ganks. Wukong is strongest when he gets R at level 6 and in the mid game when he completes his first core item.
notes.wukong-jungle-path: To clear faster, move between camps without letting your P stacks expire. R deals heavy damage to jungle camps. R has a long cooldown, so save it for fights instead of using it to clear camps.
notes.wukong-objective: Decide whether to start an objective fight based on whether R is available. Without R, engaging and disengaging are difficult, so secure vision and retreat. Force an objective fight as soon as R becomes available again.
notes.wukong-teamfight: In teamfights, wait for an opening to land R. When two or more enemies overlap, close in with E and use R. Time your engage so you do not go in late alone and get picked off. Coordinate the timing of your R casts with your team's crowd control.
notes.wukong-teamfight-clone: Enemies have a hard time distinguishing the W clone from the real Wukong. While enemies attack your W clone, circle around the side and enter their backline. When close to death, use W as a last resort to escape and deceive enemies.
notes.vs-wukong-clone: The real Wukong uses W to turn invisible and retreat in another direction. Avoid mistaking the W clone for the real Wukong and unloading your abilities on it. When a W clone appears, first check the directions the real Wukong is likely to move. Identify the W clone by the fact that it stays in place.
notes.vs-wukong-r: R knocks up multiple enemies at once. R deals damage based on maximum health. Spread out when Wukong's R is available. Account for R's second cast when deciding how far to retreat. Account for the clone copying R when deciding how far to retreat.
notes.vs-wukong-e: E is a targeted dash, so it cannot be dodged. Stay outside E range to prevent Wukong from engaging. If Wukong closes in and reduces your armor with Q, subsequent trades become unfavorable.
notes.vs-wukong-passive: Wukong gains more armor through P as he attacks champions or jungle monsters. Wukong gains more healing through P as he attacks champions or jungle monsters. P stacks give Wukong a greater advantage the longer he stays in close combat. Against Wukong, repeatedly go in for short trades and disengage instead of taking extended duels.
notes.vs-wukong-mr: Champions focused on magic damage can come out far ahead in early trades against Wukong. If your champion focuses on magic damage, fight back aggressively when Wukong closes in during the early game.
notes.vs-wukong-r-window: Wukong has a harder time engaging and disengaging without R. Force an objective or a fight immediately after Wukong uses R. If Wukong disappears from vision with R available, first break up your grouped formation.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-basic: Start a basic trade by pulling the enemy in with E, then landing Q. Follow up Q with basic attacks. Use Q from an angle where the enemy does not overlap with minions. Without using E first, the enemy can walk out of Q range.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-passive: The passive aura activates after landing three abilities or basic attacks on enemy champions or jungle monsters. Weave a basic attack between E and Q to activate the passive aura in time. When the passive aura activates, your movement speed increases, making it easier to chase.
notes.mordekaiser-combo-w: On activation, W converts stored damage dealt and taken into a shield. Use W's shield after exchanging damage. W's stored amount decays over time. Recasting W heals you for a percentage of the remaining shield. If you will not take more damage, recast W to heal while the shield is still large.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-duel: R takes one target into another realm, forcing a one-on-one duel for its duration. Neither side's allies can intervene inside R. R steals a portion of the target's key stats. R's stat steal gives you a chance to win duels against enemies who are hard to beat outside it.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-target: Mordekaiser relies heavily on his choice of R target. Taking an enemy frontliner with R leaves your allies to face the remaining enemy damage dealers. Taking an enemy damage dealer with R leaves your allies to face the remaining frontline. Among targets you can kill within R's duration, choose the most important champion in the enemy composition. Exclude high-health frontliners and enemies with instant-cast invulnerability from your R targets.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-defense: Protect your allies by taking an enemy diver into R as soon as they reach an allied damage dealer. Killing the target inside R lets you keep the stolen stats until they respawn.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-r-cast: R is a short-range targeted ability. Use R immediately after pulling the enemy in with E. Use Flash to close the distance and cast R. Use R on a clear target rather than holding it until you miss the chance to cast it.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-e: E passively provides magic penetration even without being cast. Do not delay putting skill points into E to increase your overall damage. E pulls all enemies within its area. In teamfights, use E to pull multiple enemies into Q and passive aura range.
notes.mordekaiser-skill-q: Q deals greatly increased damage when it hits a single target. When trading in lane, avoid minions and hit only the enemy champion with Q. When using Q to clear waves, account for giving up its single-target damage bonus. Do not try to trade and farm with the same Q.
notes.mordekaiser-phase: Start looking for trades from level 3 onward, when you have both E and Q. Look for kills in lane once you learn R at level 6. Use R for clear kill opportunities rather than forcing early dives. Late in the game, R can isolate only one enemy, so its impact varies greatly with the enemy composition.
notes.mordekaiser-laning-melee: Start a trade by pulling a melee opponent with E as they step forward to last-hit. Stay close to melee opponents, weaving in basic attacks until the passive aura activates. Keep pressuring melee opponents once the passive aura activates.
notes.mordekaiser-laning-ranged: Do not push the wave against ranged opponents. Farm safely with Q against ranged opponents. Mordekaiser has no mobility ability, so forcing an approach against ranged opponents can easily cost him health. Against ranged opponents, fight back with R after level 6 in coordination with your jungler's gank.
notes.mordekaiser-teamfight: Use E to group multiple enemies in teamfights. In teamfights, hold your ground among enemies with the passive aura active. Cast R on a key enemy champion after they use their main abilities. Choose your initial entry position carefully, as having no mobility ability makes it hard to retreat and re-engage.
notes.mordekaiser-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, choose Morellonomicon for healing reduction. The passive aura's continuous damage makes it easy to maintain Morellonomicon's healing reduction. Morellonomicon's healing reduction is especially effective when forcing a duel inside R.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-r: If you are caught in R, your allies cannot help you for its duration. R steals some of your stats, so you can lose a duel you would win outside it. Do not enter Mordekaiser's ultimate range alone while his R is available.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-passive: Mordekaiser's passive aura activates after landing three abilities or basic attacks. Keep trades short, exchanging only one or two hits before backing off to prevent the passive aura from activating. Once the passive aura activates, limit the time you spend fighting up close.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-w: The more damage Mordekaiser deals and takes, the larger the shield he gains from W. Mordekaiser can convert his remaining W shield into healing. Focus your damage after his W shield wears down or is converted into healing.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-e: E pulls all enemies within its area at once. In narrow passages or tight formations, multiple players can be pulled by E and hit by both Q and the passive aura. Spread out from your allies when standing in front of Mordekaiser.
notes.vs-mordekaiser-mobility: Mordekaiser has low mobility because he has no mobility ability. Use slows and maintain distance to fight outside Mordekaiser's E range. Once Mordekaiser backs off, he struggles to close the distance again. Prioritize a position where Mordekaiser cannot catch you over dealing more damage.
notes.nasus-combo-basic: Use W → E → Q in fights. Lowering armor with E before landing Q deals more damage than using Q first.
notes.nasus-skill-q-stack: Nasus's damage depends heavily on Q stacks. Prioritize last-hitting with Q throughout the laning phase. Killing champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q grants more stacks. Do not miss opportunities to last-hit champions, large minions, or large jungle monsters with Q.
notes.nasus-skill-q-tower: Dealing damage with Q triggers on-hit effects. Q's bonus damage also applies to turrets. Once you have built up Q stacks, consider split-pushing to pressure turrets with your fast demolition.
notes.nasus-skill-w: W's slow grows stronger over time. W also reduces the target's attack speed. Prioritize enemy carries who rely on basic attacks when choosing a target for W. W is a targeted ability with a cooldown that is not short. Nasus has no dash, so he relies on W to stop enemies from kiting him.
notes.nasus-skill-e-mana: E lowers enemy armor, increasing Q's damage. E has a high mana cost. Using E during the laning phase pushes the wave. Limit E poke to save mana for W → E → Q when following up on ganks or fighting.
notes.nasus-skill-e-wave: Using E near your turret pushes the wave and causes you to miss Q last hits. While holding out under your turret, avoid using E and focus on Q last hits.
notes.nasus-skill-r: R increases maximum health, armor, and magic resistance. R deals continuous damage to nearby enemies based on their maximum health. R greatly reduces Q's cooldown. Activate R at the start of a teamfight to use its continuous damage and repeated Q attacks. In skirmishes, wait until the enemy commits, then activate R at the last moment to use the health increase.
notes.nasus-skill-r-objective: Combining R's health and defense increases with P's life steal lets you tank an objective's attacks alone. A team with Nasus can attempt Baron relatively early. Suggest attempting an objective when R comes off cooldown.
notes.nasus-phase: Nasus is weakest at levels 2–3. At levels 2–3, Nasus loses head-on fights against most bruisers. At levels 2–3, Nasus relies on W to fight back. Nasus becomes much stronger from the mid to late game, once he has built up Q stacks and has R available. Late in the game, Nasus is difficult to face head-on while R is active.
notes.nasus-laning-freeze: Stack safely when the enemy pushes the wave and lets you last-hit with Q under your turret. Avoid forcing a push and take Q last hits from incoming waves. Conserve mana while collecting incoming waves.
notes.nasus-laning-zoned: If enemy pressure makes Q last hits difficult, ask for jungle help or a lane swap. Without building Q stacks, Nasus struggles to grow stronger as the game progresses.
notes.nasus-teamfight: Nasus has no dash or guaranteed crowd control, making him very vulnerable to kiting. Avoid leading the charge alone; enter after your teammates start the fight. Use W on the enemy carry to hinder their movement. Use Q on enemies standing in E's area. If an enemy ignores Nasus and goes for your backline, use W on that enemy.
notes.nasus-situational-defense: Without enough defensive stats, Nasus falls quickly to focused attacks even while R is active. Even with a damage-focused build, buy at least one survival item, such as Dead Man's Plate, to withstand focused attacks.
notes.nasus-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing becomes a problem, buy Executioner's Calling to reduce it. With Executioner's Calling, even a single Q can apply healing reduction.
notes.vs-nasus-r: Nasus gains health and defensive stats while R is active. Nasus is stronger than most champions while R is active. Unless you have a clear advantage in numbers or damage, delay the fight until Nasus's R ends.
notes.vs-nasus-w: With more ranks, W cripples champions who rely on basic attacks by reducing their movement speed and attack speed. Avoid moving alone within Nasus's range so you do not get caught by W on your own.
notes.vs-nasus-kite: Nasus is vulnerable to kiting. Even at full health, keep your distance and attack instead of fighting Nasus head-on. Nasus relies on W to close in on enemies who keep their distance.
notes.vs-nasus-early-allin: Attempt an all-in at levels 2–3, when Nasus is weaker than most bruisers. Go beyond poking and bring Nasus down to half health with your first all-in. Once your cooldowns are back after the first all-in, go all-in again and aim for the kill. Take Ignite for the level 2–3 all-in strategy. Avoid picking champions with weak early games that struggle to exploit Nasus's early weakness.
notes.vs-nasus-wave: Do not push the wave toward Nasus. Nasus can easily build stacks by last-hitting with Q under his own turret. Let the wave push toward your side and ask for a jungle gank. Nasus relies on Flash to escape. Even one successful gank against Nasus can turn the entire laning phase around.
notes.rumble-combo-basic: For a basic trade, fire both E shots, then use Q. Landing the second E on an enemy slowed by the first greatly amplifies the slow and magic resistance reduction. If you activate Q after landing only one E, the enemy can walk out of range.
notes.rumble-combo-heat: In fights, enter the Danger Zone with one E shot, then use Q. Most of Rumble's damage relies on his empowered Q in the Danger Zone. Avoid using abilities blindly, and leave enough Heat capacity to activate Q.
notes.rumble-combo-r: Cut off the escape route with R, then slow the enemy with E and use Q. Drag while casting R to adjust its trajectory. Set R's final angle based on where the enemy will flee. In fights you are already winning, use R to cut off escape routes.
notes.rumble-skill-passive: Heat rises each time you use an ability. Heat decreases when you do nothing. Check your current Heat and choose your ability order to stay in the Danger Zone. If you can secure the kill in melee range, deliberately overheat to use empowered basic attacks. While overheated, the silence limits your ability to escape using abilities.
notes.rumble-skill-q: While Q is active, move and turn to keep the enemy inside its cone. Q deals reduced damage to minions. Manage Q so you do not use it all on farming when you need it for trades. Q's max health damage makes it especially strong against tanks.
notes.rumble-skill-w: W provides both a shield and a brief movement speed boost. With no mobility ability, Rumble relies on W's movement speed boost to engage and disengage. In the Danger Zone, both W's shield and movement speed boost are increased. After building Heat, use W as you close in on the enemy.
notes.rumble-skill-e: E can store up to two shots. Landing both E shots in succession amplifies the slow, letting you keep the enemy within Q range. E's magic resistance reduction also boosts allied mages' damage. Avoid standing in front of the wave after using both E shots, as you have fewer ways to approach or escape.
notes.rumble-skill-r: Draw R between the enemy frontline and backline to separate them. Once a fight has started, use R to cut off the enemy's retreat. R is most effective in narrow passages. Check the terrain in front of objectives beforehand to find narrow passages to block with R.
notes.rumble-laning: In lane, safely chip away at the enemy's health with E. When the enemy steps forward to last-hit, slow them with E and approach with Q. Avoid activating Q first if you have no opening to get close to the enemy.
notes.rumble-laning-gank: Rumble is very vulnerable to ganks because he has no mobility ability and needs to step forward to play. If you have pushed the lane too far, check river vision first. In areas without vision, save W for escape.
notes.rumble-phase: Rumble is at a major disadvantage against magic damage opponents from levels 1–2. You can take early trades against melee opponents who deal physical damage. Rumble's ability to influence lanes increases greatly at level 6, when he learns R. Rumble is strongest in the mid game as he builds ability power. In the late game, Rumble's weakness is getting killed easily before he can reach the enemy.
notes.rumble-teamfight: Find a position just in front of the enemy frontline where Q can hit multiple enemies. Avoid trying to assassinate the backline, as you have no way to dive that deep.
