Reduce the enemy's magic resistance with E to increase allied mages' damage. In teamfights, always follow your frontline after they engage.
notes.rumble-situational-mr: If the enemy's main damage is magic, buy Force of Nature between core items to give yourself more time to stay close. Rumble's damage depends on how long he survives while staying close to the enemy.
notes.rumble-situational-antiheal: If the enemy's self-healing offsets Q's damage over time, buy Morellonomicon to reduce their healing. Rumble builds up damage by continuously burning enemies.
notes.vs-rumble-range: Q deals damage in a close-range cone. Rumble has no mobility ability. Limit the time Rumble stays close to you to reduce the damage you take. Create situations where Rumble has to walk forward to trade.
notes.vs-rumble-e: Getting hit by both E shots in succession greatly amplifies the slow, making it hard to walk away. As soon as the first E hits you, decide whether to immediately create distance. If you have a mobility ability, use it before the second E arrives.
notes.vs-rumble-w: W provides both a shield and a brief movement speed boost. Focus your burst damage after Rumble's W shield expires. Once Rumble has used W as well, treat his escape tools as spent.
notes.vs-rumble-hp: Q deals damage based on the target's maximum health. To counter Q's max health damage, choose items with magic resistance over defensive items that only provide health. Rumble is prone to giving up an early advantage in lane against magic damage champions.
notes.sett-combo-basic: For a basic trade, use two Q-empowered attacks, then E and W in order. Q has no cast time, so using it between attacks or while moving keeps your attack rhythm intact. Use Q as your attacks connect, rather than activating it before getting in range. Immediately line up W with the enemies pulled together by E to guarantee a center-line hit.
notes.sett-combo-r: For an R engage combo, use E and W after landing, then finish with Q-empowered attacks. R moves the grabbed target forward in the direction Sett is facing. To send an enemy into the middle of your team, use R with your back to your allies. The strong slow around R's landing point makes the follow-up E easier to aim.
notes.sett-skill-passive: After damaging Sett, back off and wait for his Grit to drop before approaching again. Build an early health advantage to limit Sett's chances to build Grit.
notes.sett-skill-q: Q empowers your next two attacks. Q increases movement speed when walking toward enemy champions. Use Q the moment you start chasing a fleeing enemy. Use both Q-empowered attacks on champions instead of minions. Q's damage cap per punch against monsters limits its contribution to jungle clearing.
notes.sett-skill-w-grit: W stores Grit based on the damage Sett takes. W's Grit rapidly decays shortly after taking damage. To maximize W's shield and damage, use it immediately after taking a major enemy ability. W provides almost no shield when Grit is empty.
notes.sett-skill-w-aim: W deals true damage only to enemies on its center line. W deals physical damage to enemies outside its center line. Aim W's center line precisely at tanks with high armor. W grants its shield before the punch goes out. When you urgently need to survive, use W for the shield before worrying about aim.
notes.sett-skill-e: E only stuns if it grabs at least one enemy on each side. E only slows if it grabs enemies on just one side. E can affect all enemy units, including champions. Position between minions and the enemy champion to land an E stun even in a 1v1.
notes.sett-laning-trade: When trading against melee opponents, wait for them to use an ability instead of engaging first.
notes.sett-laning-ranged: Sett struggles to reach ranged opponents before learning R. Against ranged opponents, give up trading and pull the wave toward your turret to farm. Against ranged opponents, only attempt guaranteed crowd control with E and R when your jungler comes. Avoid forcing your way toward ranged opponents and losing health while out of range.
notes.sett-phase: Sett has a weak period at levels 1–2. Sett reaches his first power spike at level 3, when he has Q, W, and E. Sett reaches his second power spike at level 6, when he learns R. In the late game, Sett's impact depends on R usage because he struggles to reach ranged formations.
notes.sett-teamfight-entry: In narrow passages, pull multiple enemies into a line with E, then hit them with W's center line. Avoid frontal engages in open areas, where you can easily die before getting in range.
notes.sett-teamfight-r: R's damage scales with the grabbed target's bonus health. To increase R's damage, target a frontline enemy with health items. A target grabbed by R is suppressed and cannot escape with movement abilities. If you have an angle to move a key damage dealer into the middle of your team, prioritize disrupting their formation over R's damage.
notes.sett-situational-mr: Buy an early Null-Magic Mantle to reduce losses in early trades against magic damage opponents. Against magic damage opponents, buy a magic resistance item after completing your first core item.
notes.sett-situational-antiheal: Buy Executioner's Calling if the enemy's healing is enough to turn trades around. Sett deals damage through multiple empowered attacks, making healing reduction easy to maintain.
notes.vs-sett-w: Sett's W grows stronger the more damage he takes. Treat the moment right after using major abilities on Sett as when his W is most dangerous. If you cannot dodge all of W, move sideways to avoid the center line's true damage.
notes.vs-sett-e: Sett's E only stuns if it grabs enemies on both sides. To avoid E's stun, avoid standing opposite an ally with Sett between you. Sett's E only applies a brief slow if it grabs enemies on just one side.
notes.vs-sett-r: If Sett grabs you with R, Flash and Cleanse cannot remove the suppression. Items that remove crowd control, such as Mercurial Scimitar, can remove Sett's R suppression. Sett's R damage scales with the grabbed target's bonus health. While Sett has R available, stack with your allies to leave no room to be thrown.
notes.vs-sett-mobility: Sett relies on R to close the gap on opponents. Maintain your range and repeatedly poke Sett. When Sett starts walking toward you, retreat before his movement speed increases. Account for the fact that poke damage turns into Sett's W shield.
notes.vs-sett-mr: As a magic damage champion, look for aggressive trades around Sett's level 3.
notes.teemo-combo-trade: Emerge from brush stealth with a surprise auto attack, follow with Q and one or two autos, then disengage with W. The attack speed boost from breaking stealth makes trades started from brush stronger than those started by walking up. E's poison keeps dealing damage after a single auto, so back off instead of staying close.
notes.teemo-combo-allin: Use Q to block retaliatory autos, apply E's poison with an auto, then throw R into the enemy's retreat path to finish them off. Throw R where you predict the enemy will flee, rather than at their feet.
notes.teemo-skill-passive: Stand still briefly without taking any action to enter stealth with P. Inside brush, P's stealth persists even while moving. Breaking P's stealth grants attack speed. Set up an ambush in brush ahead of time to use the attack speed gained from breaking stealth.
notes.teemo-skill-q: Q's blind only disables basic attacks and does not block ability damage. Use Q to poke enemies who deal damage mainly through abilities. Time Q for the moment the enemy starts their auto attack animation.
notes.teemo-skill-q-monster: Q's blind lasts longer on minions and jungle monsters than on champions. When allies are clearing jungle camps or fighting large monsters, prioritize considering Q on the monster.
notes.teemo-skill-w: W's passive movement speed bonus stops when a champion or turret hits you. W's active movement speed bonus persists even while taking hits. Use W's active to move during fights. Use W to get a favorable fighting angle as well as to escape.
notes.teemo-skill-e: E adds poison to autos, dealing damage over time. Use E's damage over time to repeatedly trade with one auto before backing off. Disengage immediately if a poisoned opponent approaches to retaliate.
notes.teemo-skill-r-bounce: Throw R onto an existing mushroom to make it bounce and land farther away. Use mushroom bounces to place R over walls or in areas without vision without exposing yourself. R uses a charge system. If there is no urgency, save R charges to block a path with several mushrooms at once.
notes.teemo-skill-r-place: Mushrooms placed with R last a long time. R's mushrooms reveal enemies who step on them. Place R around objectives and along enemy jungle routes to provide vision. Use R to clear the wave when you need to leave a side lane and rotate. Avoid spending all your R charges on farming so you have charges left to place where fights will happen.
notes.teemo-laning: Against melee opponents, use your range and E's poison to repeatedly land one auto and back off. In lane, use Q when the enemy starts a retaliatory auto. Teemo is very vulnerable to ganks. After pushing the lane, place R in the river and brush before resuming trades.
notes.teemo-phase: From level 3 onward, Teemo enters his strongest laning phase against melee opponents. Even from level 3 onward, Teemo remains vulnerable in lane to poke opponents with longer range. From the mid game onward, Teemo excels at side lane play and map control through mushrooms. Teemo struggles to serve as a frontline in late-game head-on teamfights. Teemo racks up high damage per minute through damage over time and mushroom damage.
notes.teemo-teamfight: Place R in advance along enemy entry and retreat paths where a teamfight will happen. Once a teamfight starts, attack from the back with autos to apply E's poison. If you expect an objective fight, spend all your R charges placing mushrooms around the area before it starts.
notes.teemo-situational-zhonya: If the enemy team has an assassin, buy Zhonya's Hourglass earlier to survive while mushrooms and poison deal damage. Teemo has no mobility ability, making it hard for him to survive once caught. Mushrooms already placed and poison already applied keep dealing damage while you survive with Zhonya's Hourglass.
notes.vs-teemo-q: Teemo's Q only blocks basic attacks and does not prevent ability use. When blinded by Q, deal damage with abilities instead of autos or retreat until the blind ends. Auto attack-focused champions should trade right after Teemo uses Q.
notes.vs-teemo-e: Teemo's E keeps dealing poison damage even if you back off after taking a single auto. Stay outside Teemo's auto attack range until you are ready to fully commit. Once you decide to engage Teemo, close the distance in one go and commit to the fight.
notes.vs-teemo-r: Use Oracle Lens to clear mushrooms from key routes. Move as though there are mushrooms in front of objectives and in narrow passages. When retreating, be wary of mushrooms and avoid running through familiar shortcuts. Teemo's mushrooms persist for a long time, even those placed long ago.
notes.vs-teemo-mobility: Teemo relies on W to escape. Push the lane, then engage Teemo with your jungler. Build an early lead to limit Teemo's time to place mushrooms.
notes.vs-teemo-brush: Teemo remains stealthed even while moving within brush. Teemo gains attack speed the moment his stealth breaks, giving him an edge at the start of trades. Go around unwarded brush instead of carelessly walking past it. Wait for Teemo to leave the brush, then retaliate.
notes.thresh-skill-passive: Collecting souls permanently increases armor. Collecting souls permanently increases ability power. You can collect souls from units you did not kill yourself. Collected souls strengthen W's shield. Collected souls increase E's damage.
notes.thresh-skill-passive-safety: Stepping forward to collect souls leaves you vulnerable to attacks. Use W's lantern to collect souls within the enemy's range.
notes.thresh-skill-q: Q has a long windup, making it easy for enemies to see and dodge in open areas. Use Q from brush or angles outside enemy vision. Use Q when an enemy is locked into a last-hit animation or an ability cast. Landing Q grants true sight of the target. Landing Q reduces its cooldown.
notes.thresh-skill-q-recast: Recasting Q sends Thresh flying toward the enemy it hit. Do not recast Q where allies cannot follow up. Once your allies' engage is confirmed, recast Q to close in, then use E followed by R.
notes.thresh-skill-w: An ally must click the lantern themselves to travel with W. Coordinate with allies beforehand on how to use W's lantern. Use W to bring your allied jungler into lane from across a wall. W shields Thresh and the first ally to take the lantern. Use W just before enemy burst damage lands.
notes.thresh-skill-e: E pushes or pulls enemies depending on the direction you sweep. Aim E in opposite directions when engaging and when protecting allies. From behind your allied carry, sweep E outward to peel off an assassin on them.
notes.thresh-skill-e-passive: E's passive grows stronger the longer you wait after your last basic attack. Save your basic attacks until you trade, then use them one at a time. In lane, combine one empowered basic attack with E to harass.
notes.thresh-skill-r: R only damages and heavily slows enemies who pass through its walls. Once one R wall breaks, the remaining walls deal no damage. Once one R wall breaks, the remaining walls retain only half their slow. Position R to cover both the enemy's escape route and their reinforcements' approach.
notes.thresh-combo-hook-first: After landing Q, basic attack, pull the enemy toward your allies with E, then use R to block their escape if needed. Chain E as Q's stun ends to keep the enemy immobilized.
notes.thresh-combo-flay-first: Q and E can be chained in either order. Against an enemy already close to you, pull them with E first, then use Q at close range. Q is easier to land immediately after E disrupts an enemy's movement.
notes.thresh-combo-dive: After landing Q, recast it to engage, block the path behind the enemy with R, then push them toward your allies with E. Only recast Q to engage deep when you can immediately bring an ally in with W.
notes.thresh-phase-early: Thresh can initiate in lane and create kill opportunities with Q as early as levels 1–2. Early on, focus on forcing enemies out of lane rather than getting kills. Focus on collecting souls in the early game.
notes.thresh-phase-scaling: Thresh's late-game durability depends on how many souls he has collected. Keep collecting souls after laning by passing through fight locations and around jungle camps.
notes.thresh-laning: Secure brush first to create Q angles hidden from the enemy. If the enemy pressures the brush, back off and collect souls. If enemies pressure the brush, switch to protecting your allied carry's CS.
notes.thresh-teamfight: Choose between engaging and protecting allies based on the teamfight setup. Hold Q when your allies are fighting from the back. When your allies are fighting from the back, use E to peel enemies off your carry. When your allies are fighting from the back, protect them with W's shield. When your allied engage champion goes in first, target an enemy in the backline with Q.
notes.thresh-teamfight-r-escape: When allies are being chased, place R's walls across the pursuit route to slow enemies. When using R to retreat, angle its walls differently than when trapping enemies.
notes.thresh-situational-mikael: Against a composition that locks down your carry with immobilizing effects, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build to remove them. W and E cannot remove immobilizing effects already applied to allies.
notes.thresh-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prolongs fights, buy Oblivion Orb first for healing reduction. Thresh's abilities have ability power ratios, so he can make use of Oblivion Orb's ability power.
notes.vs-thresh-q: Thresh's Q has a long windup. Move sideways immediately when you see Thresh raise his scythe during Q's windup. When facing Thresh, change direction from side to side to dodge Q. When stepping forward to last-hit, change direction once more in anticipation of Q.
notes.vs-thresh-souls: Much of Thresh's armor and damage depends on collecting souls. Trade with Thresh when he steps forward to collect souls.
notes.vs-thresh-r: Once one R wall breaks, the remaining walls deal no damage. Once one R wall breaks, the remaining walls retain only half their slow. When trapped in R, have the tankiest ally break through a wall first to help the others escape. When trapped in R, immediately decide which direction to break out.
notes.vs-thresh-lantern: Thresh's W is used to rescue allies in danger or bring in reinforcements. When Thresh throws W, immediately use a finishing ability or disengage.
notes.vs-thresh-e: Thresh's E pushes or pulls enemies in the direction he sweeps. Avoid the line connecting Thresh and his allies so E cannot pull you in.
notes.vs-thresh-mobility: Thresh has limited ways to escape a fight on his own. Close the gap and engage right after Thresh uses Q.
notes.vayne-combo-condemn: Use Q to line up a wall behind the enemy, pin them against it with E, then build W stacks with basic attacks during the stun. E pushes the enemy away from the cast's origin. Q cannot cross walls. Distinguish between using Q to set up an angle and using it to disengage.
notes.vayne-combo-w: Time your trades around W procs. W triggers whenever attacks or abilities hit the same target a set number of times. Build W stacks with basic attacks, then use a Q-empowered basic attack for the final hit to deal both instances of damage together. Switching targets just before W triggers loses your accumulated stacks.
notes.vayne-combo-r: Activate R, move in with Q's invisibility, then build W stacks with basic attacks. Q's cooldown is greatly reduced while R is active. Use Q sideways while R is active to make your reappearance position harder to predict.
notes.vayne-skill-q: Q performs a short roll and grants an empowered basic attack. Vayne has relatively short basic attack range among ranged champions. Keep Q available to disengage instead of spending every use on closing in. Use Q immediately after a basic attack to cancel its recovery animation and reposition without losing damage. Q cannot cross walls.
notes.vayne-skill-w: W deals true damage based on the target's maximum health. W stacks build separately on each target. W stacks disappear over time. Keep attacking one chosen target to trigger W.
notes.vayne-skill-e: E stuns enemies if it pins them against a wall. E pushes away enemies who get close. Avoid spending E on simple poke in lane so you can respond to ganks. When trading with E, use it on an enemy with their back to a wall.
notes.vayne-skill-r: R increases Vayne's attack damage. R reduces Q's cooldown. Using Q while R is active makes you invisible. Takedowns extend R's duration, but it cannot exceed its original maximum. Use R after the fight starts and the enemy has used a targeted ability.
notes.vayne-skill-passive: P's movement speed bonus only applies when moving toward nearby enemy champions. P's movement speed bonus increases while R is active. Vayne is built to chase quickly but disengage slowly. Check your retreat path before closing in on the enemy.
notes.vayne-laning: Vayne struggles against longer-ranged opponents because of her short basic attack range. Keep the wave near your turret and farm to reduce the risk of ganks. Vayne is weak in the early laning phase. Play to minimize losses early.
notes.vayne-laning-trade: Only start a trade when the enemy steps forward to last-hit. Trigger W once in a short basic attack trade, then immediately retreat with Q. Avoid starting a trade if you cannot attack enough times to trigger W. Save E if the enemy does not have their back to a wall.
notes.vayne-phase: Vayne is weakest at levels 1–2. Q's cooldown decreases significantly as its rank increases. Vayne becomes much stronger in the mid to late game once she has attack speed and penetration items. Avoid falling behind early and secure time to scale.
notes.vayne-teamfight: Avoid initiating teamfights. Enter after your allies start the fight and the enemy has used their engage abilities and targeted crowd control. Draw fights into narrow terrain near walls to set up wall stuns with E. After entering, focus W stacks on one enemy without switching targets.
notes.vayne-situational-qss: If the enemy has lingering crowd control that restricts movement, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items to break free. You cannot use Q while immobilized.
notes.vayne-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing offsets W's true damage, buy Executioner's Calling after one core item to reduce healing. Vayne's fighting pattern centers on attacking one target for an extended time. Vayne's sustained attacks on one target keep healing reduction items' effects active longer.
notes.vs-vayne-wall: Vayne relies heavily on E's wall stun to secure kills. When facing Vayne, avoid fighting with your back to a wall. During the laning phase, position within the minion line or toward the open river. In teamfights, fight Vayne in open areas instead of narrow passages.
notes.vs-vayne-fragile: Pressure Vayne early to force her back. Push the lane to disrupt Vayne's farming and delay her scaling.
notes.vs-vayne-w: W deals true damage based on the target's maximum health. Building armor does not reduce W's true damage. Do not rely solely on defensive items and keep taking Vayne's attacks. W requires a set number of attacks to hit the same target before it triggers. Count the hits you take and move out of range just before W triggers.
notes.vs-vayne-r: Q's cooldown is shorter while R is active. While R is active, Vayne briefly becomes invisible each time she uses Q. Use targeted abilities the moment Vayne's invisibility ends. R's duration extends when Vayne scores a takedown. Keep low-health allies away from Vayne to prevent her from extending R's duration.
notes.vs-vayne-late: Once Vayne has attack speed and penetration items, defensive stats alone struggle to stop her. Vayne becomes harder to deal with as the game goes on. Secure objectives and turrets in the early and mid game, working toward ending the game.
notes.yasuo-combo-eq: Start a trade by using E through a minion to dash past your opponent. Use Q during your E dash. Q used during E hits in a circle around you, giving it a more forgiving hitbox than the forward thrust. Use Q during E, then follow up with a basic attack immediately after landing.
notes.yasuo-combo-tornado: After landing Q twice, your third Q becomes a tornado that knocks opponents airborne. Use R immediately after knocking your opponent airborne with your Q tornado. To save your tornado, hit minions with Q to maintain your stacks.
notes.yasuo-combo-e-chain: Chain E through different minions to close the gap on your opponent. When chasing, dash through minions and save E on your opponent. If you plan to retreat, use E directly on your opponent so you can use minions to escape.
notes.yasuo-combo-r-ally: R can also be used on enemies knocked airborne by allies.
notes.yasuo-skill-q: Q counts as a basic attack. Q can critically strike. Q applies life steal. Q applies on-hit effects. Increasing attack speed reduces Q's cooldown. Q has a narrow hitbox. Crowd control interrupts Q's cast. Predict when your opponent will move sideways and use Q.
notes.yasuo-skill-w: W only blocks projectiles. Turret attacks pass through W. Beam abilities pass through W. W cannot block projectiles that have already arrived before the wall forms. W has a long cooldown, so save it to block grab abilities or your opponent's key ranged abilities.
notes.yasuo-skill-e: E dashes through the selected target. You cannot use E again on the same target for a short time. Identify minions positioned to let you dash over walls with E in advance to secure an escape route. Before using E directly on an enemy champion, consider that you cannot use E on them again to close the gap for a while.
notes.yasuo-skill-passive: Charge the passive shield by moving. Keep moving in lane to charge the passive shield. The passive shield activates upon taking a single instance of damage from a champion or monster. Once activated, the passive shield lasts briefly before disappearing. Treat the moment right after enemy poke strips the passive shield as your most vulnerable window.
notes.yasuo-phase: Yasuo stacks Q slowly at levels 1–2 and tends to lose trades. Look for kill opportunities once you have invested skill points in Q and learned R at level 6. Prioritize surviving in the early game. Yasuo excels in the mid to late game with two or more critical strike items.
notes.yasuo-laning: Be careful not to push the wave carelessly with Q. Yasuo uses minions to approach or escape with E in lane. Only start a trade when you have two Q stacks and can use your tornado immediately. Start trading when your passive shield is available.
notes.yasuo-teamfight: Avoid being the one to initiate teamfights. Engage with R after allied crowd control or your own Q tornado knocks an enemy airborne. Before engaging with R, use minions and allies from the flank to set up an angle of approach. You gain armor penetration after using R. After using R, focus on killing the enemy backline.
notes.yasuo-situational-antiheal: If your opponent relies on healing to sustain, get Executioner's Calling for healing reduction. Yasuo tends to draw out duels. Yasuo struggles to secure kills in long duels if his opponent keeps healing.
notes.yasuo-situational-mercurial: If the enemy team initiates fights with crowd control that locks you down, buy Quicksilver Sash between core items. Yasuo loses damage while locked down because crowd control interrupts his Q.
notes.vs-yasuo-q-dodge: Yasuo's Q has a very narrow hitbox. When Yasuo approaches, move sideways instead of backing away to get out of Q's straight path.
notes.vs-yasuo-tornado: After Yasuo lands Q twice in a row, his next Q becomes a tornado that knocks opponents airborne. Watch and listen for the effects that signal full Q stacks so you can prepare to dodge the tornado.
notes.vs-yasuo-post-tornado: Yasuo's Q stacks reset when he fires his tornado. Treat the moment right after Yasuo fires his tornado as his weakest window in a fight. Start a fight right after Yasuo fires his tornado.
notes.vs-yasuo-shield: Yasuo's passive shield activates upon taking a single instance of damage. Yasuo's passive shield lasts briefly after activation. Use low-cost poke to strip Yasuo's passive shield first. Commit to a trade after Yasuo's passive shield disappears.
notes.vs-yasuo-wall: Yasuo's W only blocks projectiles. Turret attacks pass through Yasuo's W. Beam abilities pass through Yasuo's W. If you play a projectile-based champion, reposition to attack around Yasuo's W. If you play a projectile-based champion, hold your key abilities until Yasuo's W disappears.
notes.vs-yasuo-wave: Yasuo uses E through minions to close the gap. Keep a thin wave pushing toward your side to limit the minions Yasuo can use to approach with E.
notes.zed-combo-basic: Place your W shadow behind or beside the enemy. Use W → Q → E for a basic trade. Hitting the same target with the same ability from both Zed and his shadow restores energy.
notes.zed-combo-ult: Make sure you have enough energy before an R combo. Start your R combo with all abilities off cooldown. In an R combo, use Q and E so both Zed and his shadow hit the target. The R mark's detonation damage scales with the damage Zed deals while the mark is active.
notes.zed-combo-w-safe: Before using R, place your W shadow in a safe spot behind you. Return to your pre-placed W shadow immediately after the R mark detonates. Use W and R shadows together to secure entry and escape routes.
notes.zed-skill-w-double: Quickly press W twice to immediately move to where the shadow lands. Practice quickly pressing W twice for emergency escapes.
notes.zed-skill-w-cost: Treat the moment just after Zed uses W as his weakest window. Zed relies on his shadows for damage, slows, and movement. Avoid wasting W on poke when the enemy jungler is missing.
notes.zed-skill-e-cdr: Reduce W's cooldown each time you hit an enemy champion with E. Hitting multiple champions with E alongside your shadow reduces W's cooldown further. To use W again during a fight, use E freely and land it on enemy champions.
notes.zed-skill-e-slow: E's slow only applies when a shadow lands the hit.
notes.zed-skill-q: Using Q makes both Zed and his shadows throw shurikens. Q shurikens pass through targets. Q shurikens deal reduced damage to enemies beyond the first target. Make the enemy champion the first target hit by Q.
notes.zed-skill-passive: P adds damage based on the target's maximum health when you basic attack an enemy below half health. P cannot trigger again on the same champion for a while. Use at least one basic attack during the combo. Avoid staying in a fight just to trigger P again on the same champion.
notes.zed-phase: Zed is strong at trading at levels 1–2. Zed can start looking for solo kills after learning R at level 6. Zed peaks in the mid game with a couple of items. Zed's strength drops sharply in the late game as enemies build armor and group up. Build a game-ending lead during your mid-game peak.
notes.zed-laning: Zed relies heavily on energy management in lane. Hitting the same target with the same ability from both Zed and his shadow restores energy. Place the shadow before poking in lane. Avoid spending Q solely on clearing minions so you have energy left for trades and escapes.
notes.zed-teamfight: Avoid engaging head-on in teamfights. Flank from the side or rear and focus on one enemy damage dealer. Use R after the enemy has spent their protective abilities and crowd control on your allies. Aim to survive until the R mark detonates. Always keep a spot available to return to with W.
notes.zed-situational-antiheal: If enemy healing prevents you from killing them in one combo, buy Executioner's Calling between core items.
notes.zed-situational-mr: Choose Maw of Malmortius if the enemy's main damage is magic damage.
notes.vs-zed-w: Treat the moment just after Zed uses W as his most vulnerable window. Zed relies on his shadows for damage, slows, and movement. Approach after the W shadow disappears or Zed has already swapped positions.
notes.vs-zed-e: E's slow only applies when a shadow lands the hit. To avoid the slow, check the shadow's position and move outside its E range.
notes.vs-zed-r-track: After engaging with R, Zed must stick to his target and build up damage before the mark detonates. Use crowd control on Zed while the R mark is active to interrupt his combo and reduce the detonation damage.
notes.vs-zed-late: Zed peaks in the mid game. Zed gets weaker as the game goes later. Avoid giving Zed an early lead. Move together with your allies to prevent Zed from killing isolated targets.
